name: libxsmm-full512-four-step-k-loop-unroll
hypothesis: Implement the swarm-selected four-step unroll in Llibxsmm_478 and Llibxsmm_70c. Each group repeats the existing two loads, two pointer advances and four FP32 FMOPAs four times, then decrements X8 by four. Both counters start at 512, so each loop executes 128 groups and preserves all 512 updates in the original accumulation order. No cleanup is needed: these loops serve only the fixed full512 primitive; other sizes retain the unchanged fallback. Parameter mapping remains [4]=original B, [10]=original A, [16]=original C, with unchanged internal packing. This differs from the historical two-step unroll. Fewer loop-control instructions may improve throughput, but larger code and scheduling pressure may cause a regression. The measured effect is unknown. ABI, thread count, compiler flags, tolerance, stores, SME transitions, allocation-failure behavior and complete BSD notices remain unchanged. No tools or tests were run. Compilation and correctness validation remain required, including fresh inputs, input preservation, full overwrite, general sizes, tails and n<=0. Measure ten reports and ten fresh alternating paired controls with unchanged power source/settings and best-of-three timing. Report spread and comparisons against historical peaks and fresh same-mode peaks separately, without choosing comparator policy. Adoption requires min(candidate)>1.05*max(paired controls) and the unchanged held-out check. No speedup, causal attribution or goal completion is established.
